newsitem.title: NAMIBIA: NEW NAMIBIAN AGRIBANK MD SAYS NO RATE HIKE YET.
newsitem.headline: NEW NAMIBIAN AGRIBANK MD SAYS NO RATE HIKE YET.

text.p: The Agricultural Bank of Namibia (AgriBank) has not yet approved an adjustment to its interest rates, its new managing director Tjeripo Hijarunguru said in Windhoek.
"The board of AgriBank did not approve an adjustment of rates at its meeting today", Hijarunguru said at a function to officially welcome him as new managing director.
He was reacting to newspaper reports that the bank intends raising interest rates on loans to farmers by between three and five percent.
Hijarunguru said the bank was aware of the difficulties farmers faced following the most recent drought, which had decimated grazing, stock and financial resources.

He pointed out, however, that the bank also had to follow a course of monetary prudence and an adjustment of rates would have to be discussed, since the bank no longer received free infusions of cash from the government.
"Once ... an institution raises funds on the open money market, it cannot afford to on-lend at non-market related rates", Hijarunguru said, "Such a policy would invariably lead to fiscal chaos."
Well-placed sources expect an announcement of an increase in the bank's interest rates to 16 percent next month from the current 13 percent.
